mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport or national identity card copies of each beneficial owner and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or national civil register in each UBO's country of origin or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for states party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise consular legalization at the Spanish Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified criminal record certificate (certificado de antecedentes penales) for each UBO, director, and authorized compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Judicial criminal records registry in the country of residence; if issued in Spain, the relevant Spanish Central Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for foreign certificates; domestic Spanish certificates require no apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or certificate of incumbency of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or equivalent corporate authority in the jurisdiction of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; for EU corporate shareholders, certified extract of the local commercial register may be accepted directly under cross-border registry rules

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of no prior registration of the proposed name (certificación negativa de denominación social)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required; domestic Spanish instrument presented directly to the chosen notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, and domestic Spanish screening standards apply. Under Article 14 Ley 10/2010 and Article 2 of Real Decreto 304/2014, PEPs and their family or close associates are automatically risk-classified as high risk and require enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior management approval. Screening must be performed against the UN Consolidated List, EU Council Regulations 881/2002 and 2580/2001, the Spanish FIU/SEPBLAC financial sanctions database, Banco de España enforcement and sanction notices, and OFAC SDN lists where any USD clearing, SEPA correspondent, or U.S. nexus exists. Negative screening evidence must be preserved in the incorporation file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Register) — official online application channel at www.rmercantil.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be transliterated in the Latin alphabet and must be legible, true, and distinctive. Spanish or another EU language may be used, provided the words are not misleading and are not prohibited by Spanish law. Accents and standard diacritical marks are permitted; graphic symbols, coding notation, or characters outside the standard Latin alphabet are not accepted. The name must not be identical or phonetically/visually confusable with an existing Spanish company under Articles 404-406 of the Reglamento del Registro Mercantil.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España, Estado, Gobierno, Nacional, Real, Ministerio and other tokens suggesting public-office, state, or crown sponsorship; these require prior ministerial authorization
Banco, Caja, Ahorro, Seguros, Aseguradora, Fondos, Mercado de Valores and similar financial-industry terms; these require prior authorization from Banco de España or the relevant financial regulator

Entidad de Dinero Electrónico, Emisor de Pago, and equivalent EMI/PSP descriptors; these cannot be used unless the corresponding license has been granted or the application is pending with Banco de España
Cooperative, Mutualidad, Fundación, and other protected legal-form tokens that do not match the SL corporate type
Terms contrary to Spanish public order, good morals, or which may mislead as to the company's true activity
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The negative name certificate is valid for 90 calendar days from issuance. No statutory extension is available; if incorporation is not completed within this window, a new application must be filed. If the Registro Mercantil Central rejects a proposed name due to identity, confusability, or prohibited tokens, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado within one month from notice under Ley 39/2015. As a faster alternative, the applicant may immediately submit a fresh application with a distinct and legally compliant name. Any approved name reservation lapses automatically if the deed of incorporation is not executed before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered office or substantive seat for an electronic-money institution. For the SL formation itself, a registered address in Spain is mandatory under Article 9 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital, but a purely virtual or serviced mailbox cannot satisfy Banco de España's substance requirements for EMI licensing. The applicant must maintain a genuine physical establishment in Spain or, at minimum, substantive local management, compliance staff, information-technology infrastructure, and record-keeping capacity acceptable to Banco de España under Ley 21/2011.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 90% likelihood of a pre-authorization or early-supervision on-site inspection, because the entity is a high-risk licensed EMI. Banco de España routinely performs physical visits, interviews with responsible persons, and verification of systems and AML/CFT measures before issuing an e-money license. For an ordinary non-licensed SL, the likelihood would be below 5%, but the EMI license materially raises the risk.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff under Royal Decree 1428/1989; scaled by capital amount and complexity of the deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Obtaining NIE and provisional CIF/corporate tax identification, including digital certificate preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Tax adviser, gestoría, Agencia Tributaria, and local police/commerical registration support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for pre-incorporation tax identification and administrative formalities

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: EMI pre-licensing legal memorandum, Banco de España pre-consultation support, and AML/CFT manual framework design
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed professional fee for licensing gap analysis, Banco de España pre-consultation, capital-requirement assessment, and regulatory implementation roadmap; prevailing market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Spanish Limited Liability Companies Act), as amended; specifically Articles 20-22 (formation), 58-61 (registered office), 62-63 (minimum capital), and 209-230 (administration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) for registration of the company; Registro Mercantil Central for name certification; Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) for the tax identification number (NIF).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation), to be filed with the Provincial Commercial Registry together with Form 600 for transfer tax and stamp duty settlement.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid up in cash at the time of incorporation, evidenced by a bank certificate of deposit from a Spanish credit institution; no escrow account is required for cash contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the public deed of incorporation prepared before the chosen notary be executed and that the Company attend to registration in the corresponding Provincial Commercial Registry. RESOLVED: That the share capital of EUR 3,000, represented by 3,000 equal participations, be fully subscribed and paid in by the founding members, and that the bank certificate evidencing such payment be delivered to the notary. RESOLVED: That the registered office be established at the address stated in the deed and that the directors appointed for the first statutory term accept their offices. FINALLY RESOLVED: That the chairperson and secretary are jointly authorized to appear before the Commercial Registry, AEAT, relevant banks, and Banco de España to process the corporate NIF, formal registration, and the electronic money institution authorisation application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Name Certification from the Central Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry), Madrid
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application for a negative certificate of the proposed company name (certificado de denominación social). Provide two or three preferred names in order of priority. Once approved, the certificate is valid for three months and must be attached to the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: Completed name certification application Form
Identification / passport copy of the applicant or representative
Payment proof of the certification fee
List of proposed corporate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected due to similarity, submit an amended application with alternative names within the same filing; internal appeal to the Registro Mercantil Central if the rejection is disputed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a Provisional Bank Account and Deposit Minimum Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution (authorised by Banco de España)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate account in the company's intended name before the deed is executed, deposit the full EUR 3,000 minimum paid-up capital, and obtain a bank certificate (certificado de desembolso) showing the deposit and that the funds are at the company's disposal.
required_dossiers: Draft incorporation deed or proposed bylaws
Identity document of each signatory
Tax identification number (NIF provisional) if already obtained
Name certificate approval
Application for account opening and deposit documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening, approach another credit institution; if the bank certifies a blocked amount, correct the capital deposit and reissue the certificate before notarisation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Public Deed of Incorporation before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the city where the registered office will be located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding members must appear personally or through a validly appointed representative before the chosen Spanish notary. The notary will review the bylaws, capital deposit certificate, name certificate, and identity documents, then draft and read the deed. The members sign, and the notary certifies the incorporation resolution and preliminary expenses.
required_dossiers: Name certificate from the Registro Mercantil Central
Bank certificate of capital deposit
Draft bylaws (estatutos)
Identity cards or passports of all founding members
NIE or Spanish identity number for foreign members
Report of undervalued non-cash contributions (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the bylaws or required documents, correct the documents and refile; the deed execution is merely deferred until the notary's objections are resolved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF) with AEAT
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), local tax office or online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 036 (Censo de empresarios, profesionales y retenedores) to obtain a provisional NIF for the company. Submit the first copy of the notarial deed to the AEAT along with the completed form. The provisional NIF is issued immediately or within a few days and is valid until the company is definitively registered.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the public deed of incorporation
Form 036 duly signed
Identity document of the legal representative
Proof of address of registered office
Bank certificate of capital deposit (duplicate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned due to missing documents, resubmit within 15 days with the corrected information; expedited hand-delivery at the AEAT office can resolve minor inconsistencies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company with the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Provincial Commercial Registry) of the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two months of the execution of the deed, submit the first certified copy of the deed, along with Form 600 for stamp duty, to the Provincial Commercial Registry for registration. Pre-pay the registry fee and complete the applicable corporate income tax form (Modelo 200) if required. The registration is effective when the deed is inscribed, and this confirmation must be reflected in the company's records.
required_dossiers: First certified copy of the public deed of incorporation
Form 600 (Impuesto sobre Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados)
Provisional NIF certificate
Registry fee payment receipt
Copy of the bank certificate of capital deposit
List of appointed directors and their acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises defects (defectos), the notary or company's legal counsel must correct them within the administrative timeframe; a second certified copy of the deed with corrective endorsements can be filed. If registration is refused, an appeal may be lodged with the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legalise Corporate Books and Obtain Definitive NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once registered, appear at the AEAT with the registry inscription certificate to convert the provisional NIF into a definitive NIF. In parallel, legalise the corporate books (libro de socios, libro de actas, and inventory/balance sheets) at the Provincial Commercial Registry. This step triggers the effective start of corporate operations and VAT obligations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registry inscription (hoja registral)
Provisional NIF certificate
Legalised corporate books
Form 036 updating tax census as applicable
Certificate of appointment of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the definitive NIF is withheld, present the actual registry inscription certificate and a copy of the deed clearly showing the registered office; for book legalisation, ensure the books are bound and preprinted with the corporate name before submission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Banco de España, Directorate General for Payment Systems (Dirección General de Sistemas de Pago) as the licensing and supervisory authority for electronic money institutions under Law 21/2011, of 26 July, on Electronic Money.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Authorisation as an Electronic Money Institution (Autorización como Entidad de Dinero Electrónico) including a SEPA electronic money passport for EU/EEA activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) and the relevant regional environmental body
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Categoría Administrativa - Office-based financial service not listed in Annex I or II of Royal Legislative Decree 1/2016; no physical industrial installation requiring full EIA. A simplified environmental registration (Comunicación Ambiental) for the office premises may be required under regional legislation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with municipal wastewater discharge limits (typically COD < 500 mg/L, BOD5 < 250 mg/L) for sanitary use only; zero industrial process wastewater. Electronic equipment and end-of-life IT assets must comply with Royal Decree 110/2015 on electrical and electronic equipment waste (WEEE) and the VOC limits of Directive 2010/75/EU if any emergency diesel generator is installed. General waste management per Act 7/2022 on waste and contaminated soils.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (Licencia de actividad) or equivalent operational start-up clearance from the local town hall, including fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, and evacuation plan. Building occupancy certificate (Licencia de primera ocupación) for the registered office. Workplace safety and health compliance as per Royal Decree 1744/2011 and Law 31/1995, with risk assessment and preventive measures coordinated by an accredited servicios de prevención ajenos; structural load inspection of any physical data hosting room or vault area must be recorded by an authorised technician.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' (SL) is created by notarial deed and registered with the Mercantile Registry. The promoter or legal representative applies to AEAT using Form 030 or Form 036 to request the corporate NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal); a provisional NIF is issued before final Mercantile Registry inscription, after which the definitive NIF is assigned. The same NIF is used for VAT purposes; for intra-Community trading, the taxable person must be verified as an 'operador intracomunitario' (VIES) and may use an additional Spanish VAT identification number. A foreign entity carrying on taxable activities in Spain without an EU tax residence must appoint a fiscal representative with an NIE, complete Form 036 for the 'NIF de entidad no residente' (key N), and register with AEAT before commencing activities. The SL's tax identification remains the NIF; no separate tax ID is required for general employment or property tax obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. A Spanish SL is a resident corporation taxed at entity level under the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law (Ley 27/2014); worldwide income is taxable. Available election mechanisms include: (i) election to file consolidated corporate income tax under the special group tax regime when the parent holds at least 90% of the subsidiary; (ii) election to apply the 'Entidad de Tenencia de Valores Extranjeros' (ETVE) holding regime for substantial participations in foreign companies; (iii) election for special VAT groups in limited cases, subject to AEAT approval; and (iv) optional treatment under the Spanish patent box and tax incentive regimes. Hybrid mismatch rules under EU ATAD are mandatory and cannot be elected out; there is no hybrid entity classification election for an ancillary 'ramo de actividad' or temporary joint venture.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (Spanish VAT), harmonised with EU Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 — no general domestic economic turnover threshold triggers VAT registration in Spain. Any taxable person performing taxable supplies of goods or services in Spanish territory must register before starting activity. Intra-EU distance sales to private individuals, however, are exempt from registration in Spain up to the aggregated pan-European threshold of EUR 10,000, subject to the OSS (One Stop Shop) election. Non-established foreign suppliers must register in Spain from the first taxable transaction if they make domestic B2B supplies or electronic, broadcasting and telecom services without using OSS.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Two-track digital clearance is mandatory. First, large taxpayers with an annual turnover above EUR 6,010,121.04 (and VAT groups) must operate the 'Sistema de Información Inmediata' (SII): VAT record books must be transmitted to AEAT by SOAP/XML web services within 4 business days of each transaction. Second, under Law 18/2022 and Royal Decree 1007/2023 (Veri*Factu), all B2B invoicing systems must guarantee authenticity, integrity and legibility, generate a structured facturae/XML record, assign a sequential hash chain and digital seal, and transmit the issuance record to AEAT in near-real time through the AEAT API or electronic platform. Commercial software must be certified; taxpayers with annual turnover above EUR 8,000,000 must comply by 17 July 2025, and all other B2B suppliers must comply by 17 January 2026. The system includes optional QR 'Veri*Factu' stamping and mandatory preservation of the issuance records; failure to transmit records constitutes a serious tax infraction. AIF (Anti-Fraud Law) obligations also require certified 'software de facturación' with no hidden manipulation features.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, the export exemption (economically equivalent to zero-rating) is available under Article 21 of the Spanish VAT Law (Ley 37/1992) when: (i) the supplier is established in Spanish territory; (ii) the goods are physically transported or dispatched to a non-EU destination by or on behalf of the seller or buyer; and (iii) the goods leave EU customs territory within 90 days (or within the period prudently accepted by AEAT) and are evidenced by the customs export declaration. The zero-rating applies to both ordinary exports and so-called 'indirect exports' if the seller is authorised as exporter in the DUA. Intra-Community supplies to EU VAT-registered businesses are also exempt (0%) provided the customer's EU VAT number is valid and the goods are transported to another Member State. For international services, a 0% rate or exemption exists if the recipient is a non-EU entrepreneur or the service is effectively used/consumed outside the EU under Articles 69 and 70; B2B services are generally reverse-charged to the recipient. The EMI's virtual IBAN and digital wallet custody services must be analysed for place-of-supply rules: fees charged to EU business clients follow the B2B general rule (Article 69) at the client's establishment, while fees for non-EU clients qualify as exportable services when the effective use and enjoyment occurs outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA — Documento Único Administrativo) with valid electronic customs status and export MRN
Customs exit confirmation / 'certificado de salida' from the AES/ECS system showing the goods left the EU customs territory
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR or equivalent transport document evidencing physical dispatch from Spanish/EU territory to the non-EU destination
Commercial invoice and packing list containing the 'Exportación exenta' or 'IVA exento / 0%' notation and Incoterms
Inward remittance certificate (SWIFT/MT103 or bank credit advice) showing receipt of foreign currency or euro payment from the non-EU customer
Purchase/procurement contract or order confirmation evidencing the commercial relationship with the non-EU recipient
Proof of customer non-EU status (e.g., registered business certificate or residence proof) for service export zero-rating
EUR.1 certificate or other preferential origin documentation when claiming EU trade agreement relief, if applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT applies strict documentary proof requirements for export exemptions; absence of the exit certificate, DUA, transport document or irrevocable payment evidence leads to denial of the zero-rating and immediate liquidation with late-payment interest. The general limitation period for VAT assessments is 4 years, but in fraudulent refund schemes retrospective clawback may cover multiple years for which refunds were claimed. Infracción tributaria sanctions range from 50% to 150% of the tax amount and include permanent exclusion from certain refund or electronic clearance regimes in aggravated cases. If fraud exceeds EUR 120,000, criminal tax evasion charges are pursued under Articles 305 and 305 bis of the Spanish Criminal Code, with prison sentences of 1 to 5 years and possible higher terms for organised schemes. In the export services context, artificial routing through intermediaries, sham dispatch documentation, or repatration of funds offshore without economic substance will trigger the general anti-avoidance clause, transfer pricing adjustments and joint and several liability of directors under Article 42 of the General Tax Law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), functioning within the Eurosystem; foreign exchange statistical and regulatory supervision also coordinated with the Spanish Ministry of Economy and the National Securities Market Commission (CNMV) for non-bank financial activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible. Spain applies Article 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) for free movement of capital. No distinction is made between current and capital account transactions for EUR or foreign currency flows; profit remittances by non-resident shareholders are unrestricted, provided tax withholdings are cleared and anti-money laundering (AML) source-of-funds verification is satisfied. Certain notification obligations to Banco de España exist for transactions exceeding thresholds (e.g., EUR 50,000 for payments/receipts with non-residents, EUR 1,000,000 for balances) under Royal Decree 1519/2016, as amended.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline for repatriation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation for export proceeds. Spain does not impose forex surrender requirements in either EUR or foreign currency. Exporters retain full freedom to hold receipts in foreign currency or convert as needed. However, all foreign trade collections must be reported for statistical purposes to the Directorate General of Commerce and Investments (Secretaría de Estado de Comercio) via the online declaration form, and banking channels must include the appropriate statistical purpose code (e.g., Form C1 'Exports of goods').

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Client Funds Safeguarding Escrow Account
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.onboarding_viability_tier: Medium - BBVA maintains a fintech/financial-services team, but EMI reserve account opening requires a full antimoney-laundering due diligence and an in-person risk committee for entities with cross-border exposure.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Client Funds Safeguarding Escrow Account
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.onboarding_viability_tier: Medium - Santander accepts licensed EMIs, but only after sign-off from their Global Transaction Banking general counsel and a mandatory site-visit/board-meeting requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Client Funds Safeguarding Escrow Account
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.onboarding_viability_tier: High - CaixaBank has an established Payments & Fintech Banking unit; its onboarding process is documented for EMI licensing clients and provides segregated client-funds sub-accounts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Client Funds Safeguarding Escrow Account
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.onboarding_viability_tier: High - Sabadell explicitly services ELMI and EMI-licensed fintechs, offering API connectivity and an express compliance channel for entities with approved E-shape documentation.
Low - Bankinter focuses on corporate wealth and selective fintech, generally rejects EMI treasuries unless the company has a direct existing relationship and a large liquid deposit.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-high legal viability for EEA-licensed/fintech EMI providers (e.g., Solarisbank AG, PPS) to host segregated account structures for the Spanish EMI, because the Payment Services Directive (PSD2) passport permits free provision. Legal constraint: under Law 21/2011 (transposing PSD2), client funds must be safeguarded in accounts held with a credit institution in an EEA country. The Spanish EMI must maintain the safeguarding account either in Spain or in another EEA state with declared intent to Banco de España. Non-EEA offshore digital banks are not viable as primary cash custodians due to regulatory prohibition on holding client funds outside the EEA without special permission.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is nominally permitted via digital video identification (eIDAS-certified) for natural persons, but for an EMI legal entity, the practical mandate is at least one physical interview in Spain for directors with independent or shadow authority. Banks with viability tier 'High' have accepted fully remote identification where the parent company has a physical office or notarial confirmation of UBO identity, but all tier-1 domestic banks reserve the right to require an in-person meeting at a Spanish branch for licence-holders classified as 'high-risk customers' under Royal Decree 304/2014.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Completely non-resident directorship and no local agent for AML correspondence
